points.response: The accident was reported at 21:57 (F13) but the off-route segment began at 21:56 (F3), so the report does not precede the deviation; RD-4(a) requires the incident's reported_at to be earlier than the start of the segment it is said to justify, which is not satisfied here.

Band 5 (40–49 km/h) is nowhere near the band 1–2 threshold (0<9 and 10<19 km/h) that RD-4(b) treats as severe congestion, and RD-4(b) is corroborative only — it cannot exempt a segment on its own even when the band is low (F11).

RD-2 refunds the metered distance of unexempted segments, and here 4.84 of the 5.0 excess kilometres (F1, F3) are unexempted, so 4.84 × $1.41 = $6.82 is refundable; the driver's post-trip statement (F10) is a claim contradicted by the 21:57 report time (F13) and by the band-5 reading (F11), so the system records win.

We do not allege an undisclosed fee item; our claim is that the metered distance itself was inflated by unexplained kilometres, and RD-2 expressly covers RydeTAXI metered distance, so FARE-1's silence on add-ons does not answer this claim.

RD-6's precondition is an upheld dispute in the last 90 days, and the driver profile shows 1 upheld dispute in that window (F16); once this route deviation is upheld it becomes the second, making the offence repeated. Note we do not ask for the flag to decide the case — it is an add-on only.
No safety escalation is sought from our side either; the absence of threats in the complete chat and fair weather (F7, F8, F9, F14) is not in dispute and does not bear on the detour claim.

We accept the segment's measurements as stated (F3): one off-route segment, 21:56–22:03, +4.84 km, up to 1176 m off route; this concession narrows the case to whether that segment is exempted, which it is not.
Confirming our C1 on the record: the excess is real and metered — 21.6 km driven against the 16.6 km optimal route (+5.0 km), billed at $1.41/km (F1, F6, F4).

Conceded only in part: it is true the trip was metered (F6) and that extra kilometres reach the fare on RydeTAXI under RD-2, but RD-2 refunds only the extra_km of an unexempted segment, and the single segment here (F3) is exempted under RD-4 because the optimal route was subject to a reported accident, so the +5.0 km (F1) is not refundable as such.

The segment exists as an off-route segment (F3), but 'unexempted' is the contested conclusion: RD-4 (a) accepts a DataMall accident incident located on the optimal route, and F13 records an Accident on the Ayer Rajah Expressway towards Jurong East MRT, 0 m from the optimal route, lanes blocked, within the trip window 21:42–22:14 (F3's segment ends 22:03).

RD-4 (a)'s timing requirement is that reported_at fall earlier than the segment start, and the record gives no finer incident timestamp than 21:57 against a segment window that runs from 21:56 through 22:03 (F3, F13); the rider's 60-second gap argument therefore asks the judge to treat a one-minute reporting granularity as conclusive, and RD-4 (b) is corroborative only (F11 band 5), not a requirement of RD-4 (a).

The driver's statement (F10) is not the basis of my case — the exemption rests on the system traffic record (F13) — and F10 does not conflict with any gps/timeline/fare value: the driver's claim of an accident on the Ayer Rajah Expressway is exactly what F13 records, so there is no system contradiction to resolve.

RD-5 governs consent to a route change and is not a requirement for an exemption under RD-4; RD-1 exempts segments with a reasonable cause without rider consent, so the silent chat (F7–F9) does not defeat the traffic-based exemption under RD-4 (a).

The arithmetic is internally consistent (4.84 km × $1.41/km from F4/F6), but it presupposes an unexempted segment, which fails because F13 supplies the RD-4 (a) accident situs on the optimal route; with the segment exempt the refundable amount is zero under RD-2.

Agreed there is no waiting-fee or add-on dispute: waiting is $0.00 and the platform fee $1.47 is published (F6), so this claim adds nothing against the driver and removes any FARE-1 exposure in this case.

RD-6 requires an upheld route dispute within 90 days, and F16 shows route: 0 upheld; the driver's single upheld dispute is on a different category, so no repeated route offence exists and the flag_account add-on fails.
